endpoint: GET repos/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/{root}/sub_issues --paginate, for each root in params.roots; per-node GET repos/.../issues/{n} only when a child lacks body or issue_dependencies_summary (it did not, 2026-09-19)
source: josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit, gh api (real capture, trimmed of URL/avatar noise -- every field board.py reads is verbatim)
trimming_note: Fields kept verbatim from the live payload: number, title, state, body, labels[].name, assignee.login, assignees[].login, issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by, sub_issues_summary.total. Everything else (avatar_url, node_id, reactions, timeline_url, ...) was dropped -- it is not read by board.py and the repo convention is to capture the wire shape actually used, not the whole response. 'children' is board.py's own nesting, built by recursing into /sub_issues for any node whose sub_issues_summary.total > 0 (none did, under either root, as of this capture).
real_capture_shape_note: The live /sub_issues payload for #3's children DOES carry body and issue_dependencies_summary (contrary to the possibility the build brief flagged) -- verified directly, so board.py's fetch_tree does not need a per-node fallback fetch for those two fields. It still fetches each ROOT's own issue (#3, #80) with a plain GET, because a root never appears inside anyone else's /sub_issues listing.

3.title: Cockpit for the pilot
3.body:
## Destination

The three screens Joe actually uses serve the pilot. Reaching the end of this map means every
decision is settled for a cockpit where he can (1) tell the screens apart, (2) cut a list down to
what he cares about — including props, (3) place and record a bet, (4) read his own judgement back
to him, and (5) look at an instrument rather than a printed report.

This map produces **decisions, not builds**. It is done when nothing is left to decide before
someone goes and builds it.

## Notes

**Domain.** A personal Kalshi betting desk (ADR 0071). Joe is a **novice** and has asked to be
educated — define every betting/stats term at first use, via `frontend/src/lib/glossary.ts` and
`<Term>` (35 terms exist and work). He uses **phone and desktop equally**; never plan phone-first.

**Skills every session should consult:** `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` on every ticket;
`/prototype` on prototype tickets; `/research` on research tickets. Read `CLAUDE.md` before
proposing anything — several obvious ideas are already forbidden by measurement (see Out of scope).

**Standing preferences, settled with Joe 2026-08-27 while charting:**

- **"Cooler" means all four levers at once**, keeping the existing palette: visuals instead of
  paragraphs; a face (team/sport identity); a real size tier so the number is big; and motion/polish
  — with the caveat that motion on a betting screen needs a rule for where it is allowed.
- **The three tabs he cannot name stay where they are and get explained.** He chose "explain them
  where they are" over deleting, merging, or unlinking them.
- **Cut the density from the row.** He chose "cut it — show less" over "hide it behind a tap".
  *Open question, deliberately not decided for him:* whether the provenance text is deleted from the
  product or relocated (there is already a per-game screen at `/market/[ticker]`). That is its own
  ticket.
- **Bankroll: a small top-up is coming** — dollar bets, not $50+. Sizing will start producing 1–2
  contract positions rather than zero.
- **Front door: both, about half and half.** He arrives sometimes knowing the game and wanting a
  price, sometimes empty-handed wanting candidates. Neither door may be buried. Market search is
  currently a collapsed line at the bottom of the longest page.

**Facts that reshape planning, measured 2026-08-27** (full dossier: 13 lanes, adjudicated by a
completeness critic):

- The ranked picks list (`GoodChancePicks.tsx`) renders **only on Games**, ~1.8 phone-screens down.
  The tab labelled "Picks" opens `/board`, whose own heading reads "Board", showing what the engine
  **refused**.
- `/bets` ("Your bets") already **is** the performance record: his settled bets with net P&L, a
  win/loss split, a cumulative money chart, open positions, and each bet scored against Kalshi's
  close. (Figures deliberately not reproduced here - this repo is public and operator account data
  stays out of it.)
- Real money betting already works from Games, Picks, Parlays, search and the single-game screen
  (`MANUAL_ORDERS_ARE_DRY_RUNS = False`). The cap is the lesser of
  `MANUAL_ORDER_MAX_SPEND_TENTHS` ($3.00) and 10% of the Kalshi balance - and the balance is
  currently the binding one, by a lot.
- **Nothing in the app has ever described a tab.** `Nav.tsx:228-238` renders six bare words.
- **There is not one filter control in the product**, only a show/hide-rejected link on `/board`.
  `/api/slate` takes only `limit`; `/api/parlays` takes nothing.
- `--accent` and `--negative` are **byte-identical** (`globals.css:26`/`:33` light, `:45`/`:49` dark),
  so every emphasis reads as "this is bad".
- On the Games screen **270 of 335 ink declarations are one grey**, and no type larger than the page
  heading exists.
- Four hand-drawn charts already exist and **none is on Games or Picks**.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->

- [Does the Parlays tab actually serve, and why not](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/4) — **Both, and it is an availability
  hazard.** `/api/parlays` stalls past 30s on a healthy process *and* OOM-kills the API: one request
  materialises 463,866 rows (`backend/parlays.py:195-241`) and grew RSS 469 MB -> 1,026 MB in 58s.
  `entrypoint.sh:296`'s `wait -n` means that kill restarts the recorder too. The Monte-Carlo ladder
  is innocent (28.9 MB, memoised). Fix is an SQL bound; the open decision is [#22](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/22).
- [Is the odds budget exhausted every evening](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/5) — **No, and the ticket's premise was wrong in
  both directions.** The 300-credit slice bound on one of three days, at *midday*, driven by this
  survey's own 13-agent load. But after a ceiling the slate falls back to the hourly floor whenever
  no kickoff-cluster slot is open: MLB went 74.1 and 61.4 minutes between sweeps against a
  900-second staleness limit. Stale evenings are real; the stated cause was not.
- [The Games row prints the wrong team on NO rows](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/6) — **Real, cheaper than feared, and it does
  not reach the money.** `fair_prices.outcome_name` already carries the opponent and resolves on 100%
  of live rows, so no `no_side_team` column is needed — one join on `/api/board` (`routes.py:1054`),
  one field in `_serialise` (`:5583`). `ManualTicket` takes no side prop and re-derives the side from
  Kalshi's own book, so no wrong side ever reached a real order.
- [Is the prop label really just one missing field](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/7) — **No — the label is not missing, it is
  wrong.** `yes_side_team` is written verbatim from `yes_sub_title`, so on a prop it already holds
  the player and line fused into one string (non-NULL on all 911 live prop markets) — under a column
  named `team`, which the screens wrap in team sentences ("betting against <player>: 1+" where the
  word is **Under**). Behind it sits a real Picks bug, now [#23](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/23).
- [What should happen when you tap the word Picks](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/8) — **The word keeps its slot and gets a screen with no order route on it; the refusal list keeps `/board` and takes a footer entry.** Ranked list = tonight's price-comparison sheet, sorted on one stored column (`routes.py:1409`) and machine-guarded against any profit-readable figure (`tests/test_slate_picks.py`); refusal list = the engine's thirty-minute audit trail, whose every row today carries a live buy button (`SlateRow.tsx:171-181`, `MANUAL_ORDERS_ARE_DRY_RUNS = False`). Q1a *lengthens* the Picks tab's distance to a confirm path from zero navigations to two. Q2a as worded turns the suite red — `tests/test_every_screen_is_reachable.py:70` reads only `href: "…"` in `Nav.tsx`/`Footer.tsx`, so the footer entry is the link and the two in-page links are struck (`/ledger` precedent, 2026-08-24). Q3b's placement holds on code (`MarketSearch.tsx:149-179` opens a ticket, not a price) but its filtering rationale is refuted: started games, a 30-minute window and `LIMIT 100` on `suggested_contracts` are not filtering problems. **Ratified by Joe 2026-08-27:** the word "Picks" keeps the slot (the ADR 0038 rename was offered and declined), and the Footer "Also served" demotion for `/board` is confirmed with the in-page links struck.
- [The one line that says what each tab is for](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/9) — **Seven sentences settled, and none of them goes in the nav strip.** Six render as the page-top lede under each screen's `h1`, replacing the paragraph each of the six already hand-rolls (`slate:121-128`, `board:130-135`, `parlays:49-60`, `bets:69-73`, `gate:45-49`, `playbook:47-51`) — so this is eight sentences rewritten, not a surface built. The seventh is `/board`'s blurb on a fourth `Footer.tsx` SECONDARY entry. **Under-the-tab was never available**: `Nav.tsx:227` is `overflow-x-auto` and already overflows at 390px, and hover is ruled out four separate times in this codebase (`Term.tsx:6-7`, `HowToRead.tsx:5-10`, `Hint.tsx:7-14`, `slate:842-843`) — putting the Gate sentence behind a hover would be the worst choice available. **5 of 7 slots were rewritten by the adversary; all three drafts failed on them.** The residual — nothing describes a tab *before* it is tapped, which is literally what Joe asked — is [#31](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/31). **Ratified by Joe 2026-08-27:** page-top placement stands, the nav word "Picks" stays, and #31 keeps its place in map order — not pulled forward, not closed.

- [Brand red and loss red are the same colour](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/10) — **Split A: red means lose.** It was
  **three** roles on one token, not two — identity, commit-money (put there by ADR 0061 §3 in
  those words) and loss/refusal, the last written into `globals.css:29-31` as a feature. `--accent`
  becomes indigo (`#2f3d8f` / `#8ea2ff`, with a separate `--accent-fill` because the dark ink
  cannot carry white text), `--negative` keeps the red and nothing else may wear it, REJECTED
  moves to the warning ochre (which the edge number beside it already used), and panels take a new
  `--edge` at 1.69/1.86:1. Indigo beat petrol and teal on colour-blind separation from
  `--positive`, measured, not judged. Two finds the ticket did not have: **every filled red button
  fails AA in dark mode today at 3.76:1** (the test checks tokens as ink, never as a fill), and the
  cited 1.04:1 was card-vs-background, not the border's 1.30:1. Prototype:
  https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ddfe5cc4-c58c-43dd-b14e-c665050b81d4

- [Do you want your own guesses read back to you](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/11) — **Yes, and decoupled from betting
  entirely.** The ticket's premise was false: there is **one** typed estimate in the database, ever,
  and **zero** hand bets have gone through the tool's order path — the Kalshi app is faster and
  Joe is already in it, so the prompt moves off the buy path. A call is logged from a **price-free**
  screen reached from the window-open digest (the game screen keeps its price and offers no
  logging, because ADR 0065's mask exists precisely to stop the ask becoming the typed number),
  shows teams/sport/kickoff and nothing else (the consensus fair value is a worse anchor than the
  price), and is scored **at close** as "you said 58%, Kalshi closed 61%" — never with the
  outcome, because one result cannot grade a probability. One call at a time until 30.
  Pass-vs-took is free: `match_estimates` already proves absence. Two standing rulings amended:
  ADR 0044's embargo now binds the **study's own rows only**, and the $100 money arm stops gating
  logging (it never gated betting). **The build is a read, not a new scoring branch** — corrected same day by
  measurement: `/api/slate` and `markets_awaiting_scoring`'s first branch share the
  `recommendations JOIN event_links` join, so every market reachable from the digest is
  already in the closing-line scoring set by construction. Coverage at the 1h horizon is
  136/136 WNBA, 578/604 MLB, 16/16 started NCAAF. The first write-up called this a blocker
  by misreading a docstring about *hand-bet* tickers (UFC/PGA/earnings, which the desk never
  covers) as being about slate markets. Refusing unscoreable markets at log time stands, and
  is now cheap rather than load-bearing.

<!-- 2026-09-02: ten calls answered by Joe in one batched interview, each with a build now owed to tasks/NEXT.md -->
- [Which sports, and do props survive October](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/12) — **Drop props from the brief (Joe, 2026-09-02).** He does not really bet them; the record agrees — no prop tap on any day with manual spend. #23 keeps its bug half only; #15/#18 grow no props axis. Packet: `docs/decisions/2026-09-02-ticket-12-research-packet.md`.
- [Where the provenance goes when the row is cut](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/16) — **Row keeps the refusal code; the prose moves to `/market/[ticker]` (Joe, 2026-09-02).** One extra tap to learn why. Build owed. Unblocks #17.
- [What do you cut the list down by, and where do the controls live](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/15) — **League + kickoff window, a sticky bar on each list (Joe, 2026-09-02).** Not in the nav. Build owed: filters on `/api/slate` and `/api/parlays`, one shared bar. Unblocks #19.
- [Does the six-link nav survive filters and search](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/18) — **Gate and Playbook move to the footer; search becomes a header affordance (Joe, 2026-09-02).** The demotion of the interlock's screen is accepted because it is read, not acted on. Build owed.
- [Should a market-search result reach a price, or only a ticket](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/24) — **A link to the game screen alongside the ticket (Joe, 2026-09-02).** Needs an ADR 0065 amendment and the game screen's 'price visible' flag made conditional first. Build owed.
- [Which of the six components that refused colour now take it](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/33) — **`Stat` takes indigo; the four chart components stay ink (Joe, 2026-09-02).** A mark on a chart is a claim, and the accent split did not change that. Build owed.
- [What colour the real-money warning strip wears once red is scarce](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/32) — **Ochre — it is a caution (Joe, 2026-09-02).** Today it wears indigo, the Confirm button's own colour, left behind by the #10 rename. One class at `ManualTicket.tsx:478`. Build owed.
- [Where the Discord window-open digest lands once Picks exists](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/28) — **`/picks` (Joe, 2026-09-02).** It has content precisely when the digest fires; the idle-hour landing is #20's problem. Build owed.
- [/board's h1 and its new footer label must be renamed together, and the word is not chosen](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/29) — **"Refusals" (Joe, 2026-09-02).** h1, footer label and blurb in one commit. Build owed.
- [Nothing describes a tab before it is tapped, and nothing ever will](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/31) — **Nothing (Joe, 2026-09-02).** A question you have once; the page-top sentences answer it one tap late and that is accepted. Nothing to build. Unblocks #19.

**Why the desk went quiet — Joe, 2026-09-02, answering the interview's lead question: "the prices are stale when I look."** Attended buys fell 75 → 5 a day over five days with the attention slice nowhere near spent, so the staleness he sees now is not the slice ceiling. Diagnosis before build; see `tasks/NEXT.md`.
- [What the record should separate](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/21) — **21A: separate the kinds, show what is open, date the record; no backfill.** `/bets` splits combination bets from single games into two sections, adds an open-now strip (count and stake, never summed with cash), states its own first day, and reads a combo as "unsettled" until the venue settles it. Backfill declined: the settlements endpoint drops history, so it would be partial and look complete. **Ratified by Joe 2026-09-03.**
- [What the Board calls the gate's own actionable rows](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/25) — **25C: a third chip, SIZED TO ZERO.** Rows the gate counts at its $1,000 reference and quarter-Kelly sizes to zero at the observed balance get their own chip and a plain-words caption; the shared `population_counts` is not forked, the row learns its reference size. They cross into the bettable bucket on their own when a top-up moves sizing to one or two contracts. **Ratified by Joe 2026-09-03.**

<!-- 2026-09-16: nine confirm-path decisions answered by Joe in one line: 39A 40A 41A 42A 43A 44A 45A 46C 47A -->
- [The Confirm button quotes a price that is not what leaves your account](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/39) — **A.** Fee on the Confirm button as an all-in figure, break-even on the line above it, both server-computed. Needs a one-paragraph ADR 0062 amendment: a fee is the venue's charge, not the tool's opinion.
- [The ticket's ask has no age, and your limit is pinned to the price you opened it at](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/40) — **A.** Age beside each ask, ticking, plus a re-read-the-book button that refreshes the price and re-pins the limit. Informs, never blocks.
- [The sentence you tick a box to affirm before a combo bet is one this repo falsified](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/41) — **A.** The checkbox reads: I understand I may not be able to get out of this bet, and any way out is small and unmeasured. ParlayCards gets the same correction; the missing test ships with it.
- [Nothing at the moment of a bet tells you the game has started](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/42) — **A.** One in-play line in the ticket above Confirm, and started rows marked on Picks. commence_ms joins the manual-ticket payload.
- [The hedge screen's headline says lock and whichever way, and CLAUDE.md says to refuse those words](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/43) — **A.** Drop lock and whichever way from the hedge headline; call it about $X either way, an estimate, with the uncertainty beside the number. The stale roughly-a-cent caveat is corrected to the 2026-09-15 census counts.
- [When the ticket refuses you, it gives you no way to Kalshi](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/44) — **A.** kalshiMarketUrl link in both refusal states and in the open ticket beside the depth line, not styled as a button.
- [The not-tonight control is missing from the screen the money leaves from](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/45) — **A.** TonightStrip on /market/[ticker]. The map's fog entry is edited to say the money-context half is built.
- [Today's realised Kalshi P&L is computed on every ticket open and shown to nobody](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/46) — **C.** Stop computing venue_daily_pnl_dollars on the manual-ticket preflight and correct the comment that says it is shown.
- [Picks goes blank on the ask in exactly the state it should shout](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/47) — **A.** A stale Picks row says the age and the remedy instead of ask not current.

## Not yet specified

- **What a props view actually contains** — a separate screen, a filter on the existing lists, or a
  per-game tap. Depends on which sports survive October.
- **The 768–1280px windowed browser.** Every measurement taken so far was at 320, 390 or 1440. That
  band is where the shell is still narrow but the wide row layout has not switched on.
- **What the record should separate.** Most settled bets are combination markets rather than
  single games, the record starts partway through August with nothing before it, open positions are
  structurally absent, and a parlay never gets a result of any kind. Sharpened 2026-09-01 by [#11](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/11):
  the record now also has to separate **logged calls from placed bets**, and within calls,
  **pre-game from in-play** — different skills that must never share a denominator. That is
  [#21](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/21)'s question and it is no longer fog.
- **Whether a small top-up changes what is worth designing.** Sizing crosses from zero to 1–2
  contracts; nobody has looked at what that makes visible.

- **Whether automated page-loads should count against the odds attention slice.** This survey's own
  13 agents consumed a full day's 300-credit ceiling by midday. The slice cannot tell an agent's
  fetch from Joe looking at his phone.

- **Whether the money line and the “not tonight” control belong on every screen a bet can start
  from.** *2026-09-16: the money line already is — `GET /api/exposure` feeds the exposure line on every surface; the control half is #45, answered A.* `/market/[ticker]` is where the money actually moves and carries no bankroll context at
  all until the ticket is opened, where the cap appears as an authorisation (“authorises 2
  contracts”, `ManualTicket.tsx:459-467`) rather than as a limit. [#8](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/8) makes the picks screen carry the
  envelope; nobody has ruled on the screen with the confirm button on it.
- **Whether the daily-loss line can bind inside an evening.** It reads realised P&L off
  `venue_settlements` (`backend/bets.py:431-456`, ADR 0064), so while tonight's games are unsettled
  its number cannot move. The only thing binding within a session is the manual exposure cap — and
  `filled` is not in `TERMINAL_STATUSES` (`backend/store/orders.py:105`) and nothing ever updates a
  manual row after its outcome (`manual_orders.py:317`), so that cap is a lifetime ratchet by schema
  accident, roughly four hand bets ever at the observed balance. Undocumented as such it will read
  as a bug the first time it fires mid-slate, and the obvious fix deletes the only in-session brake.
- **Whether a screen may host a credit-spending control as its empty state.** `RefreshOddsPanel`
  measures 961px at 390 and grows per sport, and [#8](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/8) rules it stays on Games — but [#20](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/20) has to
  draw an empty picks night whose one useful action is exactly that button. The general rule (may an
  “act to make this non-empty” control ever *be* the empty state) is unowned, and it recurs on every
  screen that can be starved.

- Nothing measures whether a page-top lede is read. The placement was decided on physics (the
  nav row cannot carry text, hover is ruled out) and on the reachability tests, not on any
  evidence about where Joe's eye goes when he arrives at a screen he has never opened.
- The Games lede appends the server's own `{data.note}` after the new sentence. Combined length
  on a 390px phone is untested, and the new sentence is longer than the one it replaces.
- The picks block's ranked list can legitimately be empty on a cold open (odds/timing.py:480-487
  against MAX_ODDS_AGE_S = 900). "One line for each game the desk could price" is true of the
  empty case in principle — the exclusions render in words — but nobody has read /picks cold,
  because /picks does not exist yet.
- Whether "the desk" (six page ledes) versus "the engine" (footer blurb) reads as one voice or
  as two products. The rule is stated and defensible; it has not been tested on a reader.
- The board blurb's "each under the named rule that stopped it" is exactly true of the rejected
  bucket only; expired and no_edge rows render named states with suppressed_reason NULL
  (routes.py:1084-1089). "Nearly all are refused" is the hedge, and the phrase is kept because
  #8 authored it as the definition of what the screen is. If exactness is later preferred over
  agreement with #8, "each under the reason that stopped it" is the one-word fix.

## Out of scope

- **Ordering or filtering any screen by the Kalshi-vs-consensus gap.** Measured negative
  (`beta = -0.141`); ranking by it puts the least trustworthy rows on top. ADR 0071 §2.5, and the
  2026-08-20 convening which dropped "any sort control" by name.
- **A win rate, hit rate, streak, average or trend line over his own bets** until there are ≥30
  scored bets with the per-group view alongside. `/bets` is "a bank statement, not a report card".
- **A bet slip that collects picks across screens.** Rejected by name in ADR 0073.
- **Making the `/board` card grid look better.** It has never rendered a card on live and cannot
  until a row sizes above zero contracts.
- **Anything that removes the typed probability, the typed order token, or the ten-minute rest after
  an order.** Those three are the entire anti-impulse structure of an armed, real-money path.
- **A hosted copy friends can visit.** Kalshi Developer Agreement §3.1.
- **Reopening the hunt for an edge**, or justifying any change by "it improves edge detection".
  ADR 0038; no screen may lead with an edge count as its headline (ADR 0062).
- **`/dashboards`.** Returns 503 on live; nothing builds the warehouse it needs; linked from nowhere.
- **Adding a seventh top-row nav link without removing one.** Asserted by a test
  (`tests/test_every_screen_is_reachable.py:125`, on `Nav.tsx` as raw text). The “pushes Gate off the
  row at 390px” half is prose in seven places and measured nowhere — at 390 the link already
  off-screen is **Playbook**; at 320 both Gate and Playbook are. [#8](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/8) is a **swap**, not an
  addition, and stays at six; [#18](https://github.com/josephsapinoso/kalshi-cockpit/issues/18) is re-scoped to whether six survives at 320 at all.

- **Deleting `/board`.** `Footer.tsx`'s docstring says a page not worth a nav slot or a footer entry
  belongs in a delete commit, and the blurb is the honest test of that — but three components have
  `/board` as their only caller (`HowToRead`, `WindowBanner`, `WindowSchedule`), and deleting it
  without homes for them recreates this repo's named built-but-never-called defect.
- **Raising `/api/slate`'s row limit for the picks screen.** The route accepts `le=500` and
  `fetchSlate` sends no params, so it is a frontend one-liner — but `/api/slate` runs an N+1 into
  `kalshi_quotes`, one query per returned row, and nobody has measured five times that against the
  0.38s warm / 5.94s cold baseline. `/picks` carries the truncation sentence instead.
- **Mounting `MarketSearch` on the promoted picks screen.** It is the affordance that turns “nothing
  ranked tonight” into “find something to bet”. Two hosts (Games and the game screen) is the current
  state and stays the number.
- **Any ordering of the picks screen other than `fair_probability` descending**, and any composite of
  it with another column. The server sorts on one stored, unscored column (`routes.py:1409`, `:1442`)
  and the screen renders that ranking without adding to it (ADR 0067).
- **Restoring “Actionable, ever” to the Games stat row.** The whole-record numbers are already in the
  slate payload and unrendered (`routes.py:1603-1604`), but the 2026-08-22 every-page review cut them
  from Games on Joe's approval as apparatus a bettor cannot act on tonight, after they pushed the
  first game row ~1,700px down. Reversing a dated, approved decision needs its own argument. The
  sentence stays on `/board`.

- Rewriting the five steps themselves — that is #19, still needed. The Playbook sentence is
  written to be true of the guide before and after that rewrite.
- FiveStepTest.tsx:170-172's claim that the negative-edge result "is on this page". It is not —
  SignalStrip renders on Games and /board only. Inside #19's scope.
- Bounding /api/parlays or gating the tab (#4, #22). The Parlays sentence makes no availability
  claim precisely so it does not depend on how #22 resolves.
- Any shared PageHeader component. All six ledes already exist, hand-rolled with four different
  class strings; this is eight sentences rewritten, not a surface built.
- A first-run, onboarding or help surface. None exists anywhere in frontend/src and constraint 7

children.title: Does the Parlays tab actually serve, and why not
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Two independent measurements on 2026-08-27 found `/api/parlays` failing to answer inside 30 seconds on five separate attempts (23:24Z, 23:26Z, 23:31Z, 23:38Z, 23:39Z), spanning a container restart. In the same seventeen minutes the Fly machine was OOM-killed twice (23:26:43Z, 23:43:34Z) on a 2GB box. Three other lanes read the source and inferred the route works fine.

**The cause is unresolved and the two candidates need very different fixes.** Is the route genuinely slow in its own right, or was it only unreachable because the process was dying?

Measure `/api/parlays` latency with timing around the ladder build itself, separately from the OOM kills. Report: the route's own p50/p95 under a healthy process, what allocates the memory, and whether the combination ladder is the thing that blows it up.

**Why this blocks design work:** Joe named Parlays as one of his three useful tabs. If it hangs, no layout change fixes it, and the whole map reorders.

children.title: Is the odds budget exhausted every evening
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

On 2026-08-27 the live `api_credits` table shows exactly 300 attention-triggered credits for budget day 20260827, the last at 20:46:30Z - the `ODDS_ATTENTION_DAILY_CREDITS` ceiling. After that the feed drops to the hourly floor, so prices on every screen are stale for roughly 45 of every 60 minutes.

**Is that nightly, or was 2026-08-27 unusual?** It was also the day a 13-agent review was hammering the instance, so the review's own load is a confound.

Read `api_credits` per budget-day by trigger for every day since the attention design shipped (ADR 0071 section 2.6) - `scripts/inspect_live_db.py credits-day --date ...`. Report the daily attention spend, the hour the ceiling was hit on each day it was hit, and whether 2026-08-27 sits inside or outside the normal range.

**Why this blocks design work:** if the budget dies every evening at 9pm, then the hours Joe most wants to use the desk are the hours it cannot be fresh, and that is a supply problem no screen solves.

children.title: The Games row prints the wrong team on NO rows
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

`backend/api/routes.py:5583` emits `yes_side_team` unconditionally, so every row on the Games screen shows the YES-side team name regardless of which side the row is actually about. A NO row therefore names the opponent - and the hand-bet ticket opened from that row inherits the wrong default side.

The `side` field **already reaches the browser**: emitted at `routes.py:5582`, declared on the client type at `frontend/src/lib/api.ts:88`, and then discarded at render (zero `.side` references in `frontend/src/app/slate/page.tsx`).

**Confirm the scope before anyone designs a row.** Is this purely a render fix, or does the payload also need a `no_side_team`? How many rows on a live slate are NO rows - i.e. how often does the screen currently lie? And does the same defect reach `/board`, the parlay legs, and the single-game screen?

This is a correctness bug on the screen the whole map is about, and it must be understood before the row is redrawn - a redesign that faithfully renders the wrong team is worse than the status quo.

children.title: Is the prop label really just one missing field
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Player-prop rows already appear mixed into Games and Picks with **no label** - a prop's title falls back to its raw market code, because `backend/api/routes.py:5574-5654` emits no `market_type`, `player` or `point` field, and `frontend/src/lib/betDirection.ts:30-35` falls back to the ticker.

Joe asked to filter "picks, props, parlays" as three things. Today props are not a distinguishable thing on any screen.

**Confirm that emitting those three fields is the whole of what "see props separately" requires** on the screens that already exist. Check: does the backend know the player and the line at the point the row is built, or would it need a second lookup? Do parlay legs have the same hole? Is there a prop-specific field that a filter would need beyond type/player/line?

Report the actual change surface, so the filter ticket can be scoped against a fact rather than a guess.

children.title: What should happen when you tap the word Picks
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

**This is the hinge of the whole map.** Every other nav question resolves downstream of it.

Today: a ranked list of tonight's likely winners exists in `GoodChancePicks.tsx`, imported at exactly two places, both on `/slate` - so it renders **only on the Games tab**, roughly 1.8 phone-screens down, behind a large odds-refresh panel. The tab labelled **Picks** opens `/board`, whose own `<h1>` reads "Board", and what it shows is the engine's list of everything it **refused** to bet.

So the word "Picks" currently opens the one screen in the product guaranteed to contain none.

Settle with Joe which it is:

- Move the ranked list onto Picks and stop showing the refusal list there
- Leave the list on Games and swap the two tab names
- Merge them into one screen and go from six tabs to five
- Leave the routing alone and fix it with a description under each tab name

Joe has already said he arrives **half the time knowing his game and half the time wanting to be told** - so whatever this becomes must not bury market search, which today is a collapsed line at the bottom of the longest page. Bring that into the conversation.

Use `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`. The answer names what each of these two screens **is**, not just where it lives.

children.title: The one line that says what each tab is for
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

`frontend/src/components/Nav.tsx:228-238` renders each nav item as a bare word - no tooltip, no subtitle, no description of any kind. The only route descriptions anywhere in the product are three footer blurbs (`Footer.tsx:57,:69,:79`) covering `/estimate`, `/hedge` and `/ledger` - three routes Joe never asked about.

Joe: *"i havent the faintest clue what the other tabs are for."* That is not a comprehension failure. **The app never said.**

He has chosen to keep all six tabs and explain them in place, so this is the cheapest item in the entire dossier and it is worth settling regardless of which way the Picks question goes.

Produce **one sentence per tab**, written for someone who has never traded, defining every term at first use (the `<Term>` glossary already carries 35 definitions). Cover all six: Games, Picks, Parlays, Your bets, Gate, Playbook.

Two of them need care:
- **Your bets** is the performance record Joe asked for and did not know he had. Its sentence has to make that unmistakable.
- **Gate** is a safety interlock for an automated path that has never placed an order. Its sentence must not imply the tool is about to start trading on its own.

Also decide **where** the sentence lives: under the tab, at the top of the page, or both. Joe uses phone and desktop equally, and the nav row already scrolls at 390px.

children.title: Brand red and loss red are the same colour
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

`--accent` and `--negative` are **byte-identical** in both themes: `globals.css:26` vs `:33` (light) and `:45` vs `:49` (dark). Verified directly.

The consequence is structural, not cosmetic: **every attempt to emphasise anything has been reading as "this is bad."** On the Games screen the single loudest element is a red suppressed row - the one row Joe must not bet. The eye is pulled to the trap.

Compounding it: 270 of 335 ink declarations on that screen are one grey, and card edges sit at about 1.04:1 against the page background - effectively invisible.

Joe likes the palette and wants it kept. So this is not a re-theme; it is **separating two meanings that currently share one token**.

Build a cheap side-by-side prototype - a real Games row and a real Picks card, in both themes - showing candidate splits:
- a structural/brand colour that is not red at all
- a red reserved exclusively for loss and refusal
- a visible surface/border token so panels have edges

Every candidate must carry its **computed contrast ratios** against both backgrounds; the existing numbers were one lane's own uncited arithmetic and must be recomputed from scratch. Use `/prototype`. Joe reacts to pictures, not hex values.

children.title: Do you want your own guesses read back to you
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Before every hand bet Joe types his honest percent chance the market ends YES. It is stored on every row. **Nothing has ever read it back.**

This is the one skill measurable in tens of bets rather than thousands, and it is the most direct possible answer to *"learn how i could do better along the way."*

It also has a real cost, and he should hear it before choosing: **once he can see the score, it changes what he types.** A number written to be graded is not the same number as one written honestly.

And there is a hard rule in the way: no average, win rate, hit rate, streak or fitted trend over his own bets until there are at least 30 scored ones, with the per-group view alongside (`backend/bets.py:169-178`, `docs/reviews/2026-08-21-items-2-3-ruling.md:119-122`). So early on this can only ever be **one bet at a time** - "your number was closer than Kalshi's price, or it wasn't" - never a scoreboard.

Settle: does he want it, does he want it held back until it means something, or does he want the prompt to stop asking him for a number at all? And if yes - where does the per-bet verdict appear, given that it can never aggregate?

children.title: Which sports, and do props survive October
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Every player prop the tool can price is **baseball**: `backend/kalshi/props.py:69-75` lists KXMLBKS, KXMLBTB, KXMLBHIT, KXMLBHR, KXMLBRBI and nothing else. Baseball ends in roughly five weeks. Football starts within days.

So "filter props" is meaningless after about 1 October unless someone decides which sports' props to add - and each sport is setup work plus roughly 12-14 odds credits every time he taps for one game, against a daily ceiling that may already be binding (see the odds-budget ticket).

Settle with Joe: which sports does he actually bet, does he want props for them, and is he willing to spend the per-tap credit cost to have them? A legitimate answer is **"I do not really bet props - drop them from the brief"**, which would remove a fifth of the stated need and shrink this map.

Also settle the seasonal question the record has never answered: `backend/kalshi/combos.py` carries an open calendar caveat because NBA and NFL were the only sports absent from the original combination capture. If football props are wanted, that caveat becomes load-bearing.

children.title: Nav.tsx's own history is wrong about two deleted routes
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

`frontend/src/components/Nav.tsx` carries a long header comment that the project treats as the authoritative record of every navigation change ever made. It asserts **three times** (at :22, :29-31 and :37) that `/builder` and `/rejections` are "still served".

Correct the comment to say the two routes were deleted, and note it in `tasks/lessons.md` as the pattern - **a comment that records history decays into a claim about the present** - not as the incident.

children.title: CLAUDE.md's headline actionable figure is stale
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

`CLAUDE.md` leads with a re-audit dated 2026-08-23 reporting **11 actionable rows across 6 distinct games**. The live instance now reports a materially larger `actionable_total`.

Three different quantities are in circulation and the survey found lanes conflating all three: the 2026-08-23 audit's row count, the Gate screen's game count, and `slate.actionable_total` (`routes.py:1176`, a **lifetime row** count where `suppressed_reason IS NULL AND reference_contracts > 0`). They are not the same number and never were.

Re-run the audit on the gate's own predicate (`gate.py:330`), record the current figure and the date, and state plainly which quantity each number is.

**This is exactly the failure CLAUDE.md itself warns about** - "repetition of a measurement, not a measurement" - and it is now happening to the paragraph that contains the warning. Every session that reads CLAUDE.md quotes this figure.

children.title: What do you cut the list down by, and where do the controls live
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

**There is not one filter control in the product.** The only thing resembling one is a show/hide-rejected link at `frontend/src/app/board/page.tsx:44`. `/api/slate` accepts only `limit` (`routes.py:1187-1191`); `/api/board` accepts `include_suppressed` and `limit` (:922-933); `/api/parlays` accepts nothing at all (:2641).

Meanwhile the Games list runs dozens of rows with kickoffs from three hours out to **eight days** out, under a heading about tonight.

So Joe's number-one stated need - "making it easy to filter picks, props, parlays" - has nothing to make easier. It has to be built.

Settle **what the cuts are** and **where the controls live**:
- by league or sport
- by kickoff window ("next three hours")
- hide what the engine already refused
- by market type once props are labelled

League and kickoff time are free - the data is already on every row. Props depend on the prop-field ticket. **Ranking or filtering by the Kalshi-vs-consensus gap is out of scope** and must not be offered: it measured negative, so sorting by it puts the least trustworthy rows on top.

Then decide the harder half: do filters live in the nav (which is at its six-link budget), as a sticky bar on each list, or as a per-screen control? Joe uses phone and desktop equally and arrives half the time already knowing his game.

children.title: Where the provenance goes when the row is cut
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Joe chose **"cut it - show less"** over "hide it behind a tap" when shown that the Games screen runs 11,974px at 390px - about fourteen phone-screens for eleven games. Just under half that height is explanatory prose.

**But every one of those paragraphs was written to stop a specific misreading that actually happened**, and they are also how the tool explains *why* a pick was refused - which collides directly with "learn how i could do better".

He was told that when he answered, and he answered anyway. So the decision to cut the row is his and stands. What is **not** settled - and must not be settled for him - is whether the provenance is **deleted from the product** or **relocated**. There is already a per-game screen at `/market/[ticker]` with no nav link at all, which is a natural home for it.

Settle: what stays on the row, what moves to the game screen, what is deleted outright. Pay specific attention to the suppression reasons (`stale_odds`, `too_few_books`, `no_market_width`, `suspicious_edge`, `insufficient_depth`, `wide_market`, `stale_kalshi_quote`) - a beginner who cannot see why a row was refused cannot learn from the refusal.

children.title: The size tier: what gets to be big
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Measured on the rendered Games screen: **no type larger than the page heading exists anywhere** - zero `text-base`, `text-lg`, `text-xl`, `text-3xl`, `text-4xl` or `text-5xl` declarations. Every row is the same weight as every other row, and the number Joe came for is the same size as the sentence explaining it.

That, not the palette, is why it reads as a printed report rather than an instrument. Joe likes the colours; he called it boring.

Once the colour split is settled and the row's content is decided, build a prototype that establishes **a real size tier**: what is allowed to be big, what is allowed to be bold, what recedes to grey. Draw it as an actual Games row and an actual Picks card, at 390px and at desktop, in both themes.

Two things to bring in that already exist and are currently parked on screens Joe never opens:
- four hand-drawn chart components (`RecordChart`, `PriceChart`, `FairValueSteps`, `ParlayDifficulty`) - **none of them renders on Games or Picks**
- the tick-up/tick-down motion CSS, which does reach `/board` via a runtime-interpolated class at `LiveBoard.tsx:267`

Joe asked for motion and polish. Settle **where motion is allowed** as part of this: a betting screen that celebrates is how a casino makes you act, and this product's own rulings forbid manufacturing action.

children.title: Does the six-link nav survive filters and search
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

The top row holds exactly six links and the count is a hard budget: a seventh pushes Gate - the screen that says whether money can move - off the row at 390px, and a test asserts it.

Joe has decided all six current tabs stay and get explained rather than removed. But this map is going to want to add: filter controls, a first-class market search (he arrives half the time already knowing his game, and search is currently a collapsed line at the bottom of the longest page), and possibly a props view.

**Something has to give, and it is his call which.** The candidates, all of which have precedent - seven routes are already served-but-unlinked:
- Gate and Playbook move to the footer, which currently carries only three links against six in the nav
- search becomes a persistent affordance in the header rather than a nav slot
- filters live on the screens rather than in the chrome
- the budget of six is itself revisited

Bring the actual measurement: what the row does at 390px with seven items, and what the footer looks like at 6-and-3 today.

children.title: Rewrite the five-step guide against the app that exists
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

The five-step pre-bet test (`frontend/src/components/FiveStepTest.tsx`, rendered only at `/playbook`) is the best beginner writing in the product - and its **first instruction is impossible to follow.**

- Step 1 (`:33`, verbatim): *"Open Log, tap the market, and type your P(YES)"*. The Log tab was retired from the nav on 2026-08-21 and the form it pointed at was retired on 2026-08-22.
- Step 5 (`:140-141`) sends him back to the same dead screen and promises a calibration score from a study **he himself cancelled without a result**.
- Step 4's *"$2 every time"* is the same sentence the glossary already deleted elsewhere for contradicting the real cap.

So the one screen serving "learn how i could do better" sits on the tab Joe understands least, and tells him to use something that no longer exists.

Settle what each of the five steps should say about the app **as it actually is** - including where the typed probability is entered now, and what step 5's stopping rule refers to given the study is over. Whether the guide stays on `/playbook` or moves somewhere he will actually read it depends on the Picks and tab-description tickets, which is why this is blocked on both.

children.title: What the empty night looks like when it is designed
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

On this project's own measurements, **"nothing worth betting" is the correct and most common answer.** Which means the version of the app Joe opens most often is the empty one.

Every survey lane treated empty as a failure state to apologise for. **Nobody has ever designed it.** Today an empty Games screen reads as the tool being broken rather than the tool working correctly - and that misreading is compounded by the odds budget going quiet in the evening, which makes "stale" and "nothing here" look identical.

Build a throwaway prototype of the Games and Picks screens in the empty state, deliberate rather than apologetic. It has to answer, without prose: *is this the tool saying "no bets tonight", or the tool saying "I could not reach the data"?* Those are completely different facts and the screen currently conflates them.

This is arguably the highest-leverage visual ticket on the map, because it is the state he sees most. Use `/prototype`.

children.title: What the record should separate
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

`/bets` already is the performance record Joe asked for. It has four structural holes, none of which is a bug, and all of which change what the screen can honestly claim:

- **Combination markets are mixed in with single games**, and they are the majority. A parlay and a moneyline are not the same kind of bet and averaging them says little.
- **The record starts partway through August.** Nothing before that exists at all.
- **Open positions are structurally absent** from the settled view, so money at risk right now is not in the picture.
- **A parlay never gets a result of any kind** - it is placed and then the record goes silent.

Settle with Joe which of these he wants separated, which backfilled, and which left alone.

Hard constraint to bring into the conversation: **no average, win rate, hit rate, streak or trend line** may appear until there are at least 30 scored bets with the per-group view alongside. `/bets` describes itself as "a bank statement, not a report card" and that is a standing ruling. So the answer here is about **what the screen separates**, never about what it scores.

children.title: Does Parlays stay up while its query is unbounded
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Resolved in #4, reproduced independently by two agents: **every visit to the Parlays tab is a ~557 MB allocation on a 2 GB box that already sits at ~1.03 GB at rest.** `ladder_candidates` (`backend/parlays.py:195-241`) materialises 463,866 rows from a rolling 24-hour window of `fair_prices` into Python before deduping. The route stalls past 30s on a *healthy* process, and repeated calls OOM-kill the uvicorn API process. Because `docker/entrypoint.sh:296` uses `wait -n`, killing that child tears down the container and **restarts the recorder too** — so the blast radius is the whole site, not one tab. A live outage of about 91 seconds was observed while measuring it.

The fix direction is settled and is not in doubt: bound the result set in SQL — freshest-per-identity, a LIMIT, or a much narrower window. That is a build, not a decision.

**The decision is what happens in the meantime.** Parlays is one of the three tabs Joe named as useful, so this is his call and not an agent's:

- Leave it up and accept that opening it can take the site down for a couple of minutes
- Disable or gate the tab until the query is bounded
- Ship the SQL bound first and change nothing else

Bring the actual numbers to the conversation: how often he opens it, and what the recorder losing two minutes costs the record.

**Take this one early.** It is the only ticket on this map where the status quo actively harms the running system.

children.title: Should player props appear in Likely winners
children.body:
Part of #3

## Question

Surfaced while resolving #7, and it is a bug behind a design question.

The "Likely winners tonight" block is built server-side at `backend/api/routes.py:1387-1443`. It groups by `odds_event_id` — **which a prop event inherits from its game** — and filters only on `side == "yes"` and a non-null `fair_probability`. Nothing excludes player props. So a prop can be selected as the representative row for a game and presented as the game's likely winner.

Compounding it, #7 established that the label problem is not what it looked like. `kalshi_markets.yes_side_team` is written verbatim from `yes_sub_title` (`backend/runner.py:3031,3041`), so on a prop it already holds something like `"<player>: 1+"` — player and line fused into one string, non-NULL on all 911 live prop markets. The field is then **named `team`** and the screens write team sentences around it: `frontend/src/app/market/[ticker]/page.tsx:242-244` renders "this contract pays $1 if the <player>: 1+ win", and `frontend/src/lib/betDirection.ts` turns a NO prop into "You are betting against <player>: 1+" when the correct word is **Under** (`backend/runner.py:1525` maps yes→Over, no→Under, and that mapping never leaves the runner).

Settle: should props appear in the likely-winners list at all, appear labelled as props, or be excluded and given their own surface? The answer depends on what the Picks tab becomes (#8) and on whether props survive October (#12).

children.title: Should a market-search result reach a price, or only a ticket
children.body:
Part of #3. Split out of #8, which settled the search box's *placement* and could not settle its *destination*.

`MarketSearch` results are not links. Each is a `<button onClick={() => setChosen(...)}>` that toggles an inline hand-bet ticket in place (`frontend/src/components/MarketSearch.tsx:149-179`), and the route serves no price by construction — `estimates.search_markets`' SELECT carries no quote column, and `backend/api/routes.py:4548-4552` records that as load-bearing rather than incidental.

So for the arrival hard-constraint 7 protects — Joe knows his game and wants a price — the desk's only door is an order form. That is the inverse of the job ADR 0071 §2.2 assigns it. It is not a corner case: the runner drops every started fixture (`backend/runner.py:1105-1108`, `:1483-1485`, `:1920-1922`; 36 of 104 rows on one live pass, ADR 0006), so after first pitch search is the *only* door to that market.

Settle: should a search result also be a `<Link href="/market/{ticker}">` alongside the ticket?

Three things that make this a decision rather than a build:

- It amends **ADR 0065**'s estimate-before-price mask on a path where the mask is current, not vestigial: ADR 0065 §1 records that the premise changed on 2026-08-22 when `bet_clv()` shipped, giving a pre-bet P(YES) a live consumer on `/bets`. This needs an ADR amendment, not a quiet edit.
- `tests/test_buy_controls.py:56` pins `components/MarketSearch.tsx` as a surface that must mount `<ManualTicket`. Any link must be **additional**; replacing the ticket is a deliberate test edit.
- `frontend/src/app/market/[ticker]/page.tsx:326` passes `priceAlreadyVisible` **unconditionally**, including when `detail` is null (`:301-310` renders "the recorder never priced this ticker") and when `QuoteStrip` refuses a stale ask. Routing search results there today moves a reader from a surface where the mask honestly holds to one that announces it does not while showing no price. If the link is approved, that flag must become conditional on `QuoteStrip` actually printing a current ask before it ships.

Also decide, since #8 explicitly left it open: constraint 7's "knows his game" half is **not** discharged by #8 and cannot be discharged by #15 (filtering cannot reach a row that was never written). Does it close here, or does it need its own answer?

children.title: What the Board calls the gate's own actionable rows
children.body:
Part of #3. Surfaced by #8 and not fixed by it — demoting `/board` to the footer makes this harder to notice, not better.

`/board` files **all 11 rows the gate has ever counted actionable** under the muted `NO EDGE` chip, captioned "no edge after fees" (`frontend/src/components/SlateRow.tsx:56-57`, `:154`) — two inches below a paragraph printing "11 of N decisions ever recorded" (`frontend/src/app/board/page.tsx:221-243`).

The cause is a partition mismatch, not a rendering bug. The Board buckets on `suggested_contracts` — `surfaced` and `expired` both require `> 0`, everything else falls through to `no_edge` (`backend/api/routes.py:1085-1090`) — while the gate's predicate counts `reference_contracts` at the fixed $1,000 reference profile (`backend/gate.py:330`, ADR 0015 §3). `suggested_contracts` is 0 on every one of the 11 (`docs/measurements/2026-08-23-actionable-population-reaudit.md`), because quarter-Kelly against the observed balance sizes zero.

Settle which number the screen's buckets are *about*:

- Bucket on what Joe can buy today (`suggested_contracts`) and say so — the chip stops claiming "no edge" and starts saying "unbuyable at this bankroll", which is what is true.
- Bucket on the gate's own predicate (`reference_contracts`) so the page and its own headline sentence agree, and let the size read as zero on the row.
- Something else, with a third chip.

Note the constraint: `population_counts(conn, 0)` is deliberately shared so the Board's number and the gate's number cannot drift (`routes.py:1176`). Whatever is chosen must not fork that.

This is also about to matter more, not less: map #3 records that a small top-up is coming and sizing crosses from zero to 1–2 contracts.

children.title: Which clock the kickoff column tells
children.body:
Part of #3. #8 promotes the ranked list to its own nav slot; the first column on every line of that list is a start time, and it is drawn from a field this repo has measured as three hours late.

`/api/slate` selects `e.commence_ms` raw from `kalshi_events` (`backend/api/routes.py:1256`) and sorts the whole Games list on it (`:1353-1359`); `GoodChancePicks` renders it (`frontend/src/components/GoodChancePicks.tsx:59-61`). `backend/match/linker.py:77-80` records `OBSERVED_KALSHI_COMMENCE_OFFSET_MS = 3 * 3600 * 1000` with the comment "Not applied anywhere", asserted by `tests/test_linker.py:364-375` on 14 of 18 MLB and 6 of 6 WNBA pairs at exactly +180 minutes.

Every other consumer already refuses it in favour of the linked sportsbook fixture's clock: `/api/market/{ticker}` (`routes.py:1647-1651`), `/api/ledger`, `gate.py:977-988`, and `_resolve_scout_fixture` (`routes.py:1744-1749`). So a 19:05 first pitch prints as 22:05 on Games and correctly on the game screen one tap later.

What has to be decided rather than merely fixed:

1. **Adjudicate the dissent.** `backend/kalshi/discovery.py:464-479` says `occurrence_datetime` is "when the game actually starts". Five sites and a test say otherwise. One of those docstrings is wrong and somebody should establish which rather than take a lane's word.
2. **Does the sort move with the display?** Fixing the printed time without the sort key leaves the list ordered on a clock nobody sees; fixing both changes row order on Games, which is a visible change to the home screen.
3. **What happens to a row with no linked fixture?** The join that fixes this is the one `routes.py` already writes elsewhere; rows without a match need a rule, and this repo's convention is that unreadable resolves to `None`, never to a substituted value.

This is a precondition for shipping #8's promoted screen: do not put a wrong number in the first column of a nav-slot screen. Answering "do I have time to act" wrong by 180 minutes costs the bet, not seconds.

children.title: The Games sort already tiebreaks on the gap the map rules out of scope
children.body:
Part of #3. Found while resolving #8.

Map #3 rules out of scope: "ordering or filtering ANY screen by the Kalshi-vs-consensus gap (measured beta = -0.141, ranking by it puts the least trustworthy rows on top)". The Games screen already does it.

`backend/api/routes.py:1353-1359`:

    items.sort(key=lambda r: (r["commence_ms"] is None, r["commence_ms"] or 0, -(r["edge_tenths"] or 0)))

This is not a rare tiebreak. Both sides of a moneyline share a byte-identical `commence_ms`, so the third key decides which side of **every** game prints first — and the side printed first is the higher-apparent-edge one. Combined with `_serialise` writing `yes_side_team` on both rows (`routes.py:5583`) and the row rendering neither `side` nor `event_title`, the top row of each pair is silently the one the measurement says to trust least, under a label that does not say which side it is.

The line predates the ticket and nobody has ruled on it. Two ways out and the decision is which:

- **Fix it** — replace the tiebreak with something that carries no claim (ticker, then side), and say in the sort's comment why.
- **Record it as an exemption** — a deterministic tiebreak inside a pair is not a ranking of the screen, and the map's rule was aimed at ordering the list as a whole.

Do not leave it undecided: the map cites this rule as a hard constraint on four other tickets, and citing a rule the code violates in the same file weakens all four.

children.title: Where the Discord window-open digest lands once Picks exists

Part of #3. Graduates the "What happens after he taps the Discord notification" bullet from Not-yet-specified, and is now answerable because #8 settled what the Picks slot opens.

Discord is the only channel that emits URLs (`backend/notify/alerts.py` contains none). Four embeds carry a link:

- `:389` — the parlay card, `/parlays`.
- `:479` — the hedge alert, `/hedge`.

The digest is the only push that lands on a list screen at all, and it fires exactly when a window opens — the moment the ranked list is freshest and most useful. Settle where it should land: the root (unchanged), `/picks`, or somewhere that names what the digest is about.

Two things to weigh:

- The digest arrives when odds have just been bought, which is the state in which `/picks` has content; the same tap on an idle hour meets `MAX_ODDS_AGE_S = 900` against an hourly floor (`backend/odds/timing.py:487`) and lands on the empty state #20 is designing.
